::: {.obsidian-technical-design}
:::

State the purpose and scope of the security architecture in one
paragraph. Name the system, the security objectives, and the
standards applied (e.g., JSP 815, Def Stan 05-138, AQAP 2210).

# System boundary

Describe the system boundary. Name the assets, data flows, and
trust boundaries. Identify what is inside and outside the control
of the system.

## Assets

List the assets within the system boundary. For each asset, state
its classification, its value, and the owner.

## Data flows

Map the data flows between system components. For each flow, state
the classification of the data, the protocol, and the protection
measures.

## Trust boundaries

Identify the trust boundaries. State where the trust level changes
and what controls enforce the boundary.

# Threat model (STRIDE)

Apply the STRIDE threat model to each system component. For each
threat, state the likelihood, the impact, and the mitigations.

## Spoofing

What threats allow an attacker to impersonate a legitimate user or
component? State the mitigations.

## Tampering

What threats allow an attacker to modify data or code in transit
or at rest? State the mitigations.

## Repudiation

What threats allow a user to deny an action? State the audit and
logging controls.

## Information disclosure

What threats allow an attacker to access sensitive data? State the
encryption and access controls.

## Denial of service

What threats allow an attacker to disrupt availability? State the
capacity and resilience controls.

## Elevation of privilege

What threats allow an attacker to gain unauthorised access? State
the authentication and authorisation controls.

# Security controls

For each security control, state the control objective, the
implementation, and the verification method. Use a table.

| Control | Objective | Implementation | Verification |
|---------|-----------|----------------|--------------|
| Access control | Restrict access to authorised users | Role-based access control | Quarterly access review |
| Encryption | Protect data in transit and at rest | TLS 1.3, AES-256 | Penetration testing |
| Audit logging | Record all security-relevant events | Centralized log aggregation | Log review |

# Risk assessment

For each identified risk, state the likelihood, the impact, and
the residual risk after mitigations. Use the risk matrix.

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Rating | Mitigation | Residual |
|------|------------|--------|--------|------------|----------|
| Unauthorised access | Medium | High | High | RBAC + MFA | Low |
| Data breach | Low | Critical | High | Encryption + monitoring | Medium |

# Compliance

Map the security controls to the applicable standards. State the
compliance status for each standard.

| Standard | Control | Status |
|----------|---------|--------|
| JSP 815 | Safety management | Compliant |
| Def Stan 05-138 | Information security | Compliant |
| AQAP 2210 | Software quality | Compliant |

# Appendices

State any supplementary material: assumptions, glossary, or
references.
